Inventive

/in-VEN-tiv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Inventive means showing skill and imagination in creating new things.

Everyone in the family agreed that Grandpa Ruben was endlessly inventive, turning old bicycle wheels and clothespins into a working backyard cable car for delivering snacks to the treehouse.

Worked Example

With the class budget gone, Ms. Otero's greenhouse club needed a way to water the seedlings over winter break. Dana, the most inventive member of the club, built a slow drip system out of recycled bottles, cotton string, and a kitchen timer, and it kept every plant alive until January.

Dana solves the problem by imagining and building something new out of ordinary materials, which is exactly what it means to be inventive.

How Inventive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

imaginative

imaginative: full of new and original ideas

resourceful

resourceful: skilled at finding clever ways around problems

ingenious

ingenious: strikingly clever and original

Antonyms

unimaginative

unimaginative: lacking new ideas

uninspired

uninspired: dull and showing no creativity

How Strong Is It? — resourceful → inventive → visionary

resourceful vs. inventive

resourceful vs. inventive: A resourceful person makes clever use of whatever is on hand, while an inventive person goes further and dreams up genuinely new creations.

visionary vs. inventive

visionary vs. inventive: An inventive tinkerer comes up with new gadgets and fixes, but a visionary imagines whole new worlds and ways of living.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: on, upon

Root — vent

Root — vent: from Latin venire, to come

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: adjective-forming ending, tending to

Put it together

Put it together: Inventive traces back to Latin invenire, 'to come upon, to find,' built from in-, 'on, upon,' plus venire, 'to come,' with the adjective ending -ive. An inventive mind is one that keeps 'coming upon' fresh ideas and solutions that no one else has found.

Use the root in a new word: advent

Use the root in a new word: advent: Fans counted down to the advent of the new gaming console, using a word that literally means 'a coming toward,' from the same Latin root venire that hides inside inventive.

Word Choice

neutral, approving

Inventive praises a person's creative quality, as in 'an inventive engineer' or 'an inventive solution.' Inventive describes a creative quality, closely related to the verb invent, which names the act of creating something new.
